transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Head of ML, Arbor), Victor Huang (Infra), Ellen Park (PM), Ravi Mehta (CISO)

Summary: Quick product walkthrough focused on evaluation/quality monitoring: prompt-sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons. Customer wants to validate that Redwood can detect regressions from model updates and support controlled A/B experiments. Security and private deployment constraints discussed. Next: send pricing and run a pilot with a 200-prompt set.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you fitting this in before the holiday week. i'm samira, i'm the AE on the account. quick intros?
00:08 Speaker 2 (Maya): sure, maya here, head of ml at arbor finance. we're evaluating options for monitoring model regressions for our customer support generator and a few compliance redaction tasks.
00:16 Speaker 3 (Victor): victor, infra lead. mainly concerned about private vpc, kms keys, and the latency envelope.
00:21 Speaker 1 (Samira): awesome, and liam from our solutions eng will walk through the console and the evaluation flow.
00:26 Speaker 4 (Liam): hi everybody, thanks. i want to show three things in about 35 minutes: prompt set management, regression alerts, and A/B compare flows in the console + how you can run a bench via the api. feel free to jump in.
00:38 Speaker 5 (Ellen): quick Q — timeline? our PM wants a pilot before end of year if possible.
00:42 Speaker 1 (Samira): yeah, that's the ask i heard — short pilot. we can do a 2-week pilot; liam will propose config.
00:49 Speaker 4 (Liam): ok, jumping to screen (notes: demo shows console). so here is the prompt-sets page — we use prompt-sets to group prompts by intent, add expected outputs and metrics. you can attach golden labels for automated scoring.
01:05 Speaker 2 (Maya): how are you storing the golden labels — any PII concerns?
01:09 Speaker 4 (Liam): labels are encrypted at rest; for hosted we use our KMS, for private you can supply your own customer-managed KMS. logs with PII can be redacted or kept only in VPC/private deployment.
01:20 Speaker 2 (Maya): okay, that's helpful.
01:23 Speaker 4 (Liam): demo — i import a CSV of 200 prompt/examples. watch how we define an evaluator that uses BLEU-ish scoring and a custom regex check for redaction. sometimes the transcript misreads the kernel name — this is the internal "serve-run" UI, in reality we call the runtime.
01:44 Speaker 2 (Maya): will the regex check run inline or as a post-check?
01:47 Speaker 4 (Liam): it's a post-eval step. we support custom validators in the console or as an API webhook.
01:53 Speaker 3 (Victor): latency — if we run the bench, what's realistic P95 for a 512-token generation?
01:58 Speaker 4 (Liam): on hosted with our standard L-series models you could expect 120-250ms p95 for short generations, depends on batch size. for dedicated or private GPU setups, you'll see consistent p95 that we can guarantee in the SLA. "p95" was sometimes transcribed as "peak 95" earlier in our docs — apologies for that.
02:17 Speaker 5 (Ellen): we have two goals: catch semantic regressions, and ensure our redaction rule recall doesn't drop below 98%. how do alerts map to those?
02:26 Speaker 4 (Liam): you create regression guards on metric thresholds — e.g., if redaction recall drops 98% for 3 consecutive runs or delta > 2% vs baseline, trigger an alert. alerts can be email, slack, pagerduty, or auto-roll back to a fallback model.
02:40 Speaker 2 (Maya): fallback model — is that a smaller open model or previous version?
02:44 Speaker 4 (Liam): either. you can pin a fallback to a quantized variant or a previous deploy tag. note: our UI will show compatibility warnings if a model variant doesn't support the KV cache schema — sometimes transcribed as vac-cache.
02:56 Speaker 3 (Victor): about A/B — can we do traffic splits by user segment? we need to route only US customers to the test model.
03:03 Speaker 4 (Liam): yes, routing policies support geolocation, headers, or token attributes. you can set percentage splits and tie each split to a prompt-set and evaluation run. we'll show the A/B compare visualization next.
03:15 Speaker 4 (Liam): switching to the A/B compare tab — here's a side-by-side for outputs, pairwise diffs, and a summary score. you can drill into individual prompts and see the exact deltas, annotate responses, and mark reversions for later analysis.
03:29 Speaker 2 (Maya): can annotations feed training data or fine-tune flows?
03:33 Speaker 4 (Liam): yes, annotations export as labeled datasets. for hosted we store them in your workspace; for private you can push to your S3 or an on-prem endpoint.
03:42 Speaker 1 (Samira): quick commercial check — Maya, are you evaluating hosted or private?
03:46 Speaker 2 (Maya): ideally private VPC because of finance regs, but we might start hosted for rapid iteration if you have a strong encryption story.
03:54 Speaker 1 (Samira): we can do a hybrid pilot: hosted control plane with private deployment and customer-managed KMS, or full private. pricing differs, we'll send both options.
04:03 Speaker 3 (Ravi): on that, SOC2 + ISO? audit logs retention?
04:07 Speaker 4 (Liam): we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001; audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM and retention configured per workspace. for private deployments you keep logs inside your network.
04:18 Speaker 3 (Ravi): good. also need to confirm HSM integration — we require HSM-backed keys for certain datasets.
04:23 Speaker 4 (Liam): yes, on private you can integrate with your HSM/KMS — we'll include the integration notes in the security pack.
04:30 Speaker 5 (Ellen): any limitations around A/B sample sizes or running weekly sims?
04:34 Speaker 4 (Liam): no hard limits, but cost scales with token usage. Optimize suggestions can recommend smaller subset sampling to catch regressions faster.
04:42 Speaker 2 (Maya): about regressions — can we run nightly baseline checks and fail builds or gate rollouts?
04:47 Speaker 4 (Liam): absolutely, you can wire regression alerts into CI. we have webhooks and a small CLI that returns non-zero on fail so your pipeline can block a rollout.
04:58 Speaker 2 (Maya): and what about fuzzy semantic drift? exact matching won't catch it.
05:02 Speaker 4 (Liam): we support embedding-based similarity metrics for semantic drift. you can set thresholds on mean cosine similarity vs baseline, and define per-intent tolerances.
05:12 Speaker 2 (Maya): do you support multilabel scorer? we have some prompts with multi-intent outputs.
05:17 Speaker 4 (Liam): yes, custom scorers are supported; you can upload a scorer function or pick from built-ins.
05:25 Speaker 1 (Samira): ok quick break for any procurement/legal Qs?
05:29 Speaker 3 (Victor): contract length — we prefer a short pilot then a 12-month committed for predictability.
05:34 Speaker 1 (Samira): that matches our typical path. we'll provide reserved capacity and a committed option.
05:38 Speaker 2 (Maya): one last big concern — explainability. our compliance needs a trail of why a model produced a certain redaction.
05:46 Speaker 4 (Liam): we keep per-request trace logs with token-level scoring and the evaluation trace. those can be sampled and included in the audit export; in private deployments those never leave your VPC.
05:58 Speaker 5 (Ellen): can we demo a baseline run on a small set now?
06:02 Speaker 4 (Liam): we can do a quick run — i'm going to trigger a 20-example run via the API to show metrics. starting run... (console shows progress)
06:20 Speaker 4 (Liam): run complete — summary: 20 prompts, redaction recall 99%, semantic sim mean 0.92, aggregate score 0.87. note: these are synthetic examples.
06:33 Speaker 2 (Maya): nice. how do we record a regression alert rule?
06:36 Speaker 4 (Liam): i'll create a rule here: metric = redaction_recall, condition = below 0.98 for 2 runs, action = slack + rollback to tag v1.2.
06:49 Speaker 2 (Maya): can rollback be manual? we want human-in-loop for finance.
06:52 Speaker 4 (Liam): yes, you can choose automatic or manual. default is manual for enterprise.
06:57 Speaker 3 (Victor): about data residency — our EU customers must stay in eu-region. can rules be region-specific?
07:03 Speaker 4 (Liam): routing and evaluation are region-aware; you can scope prompt-sets to a region or apply regional policies.
07:10 Speaker 2 (Maya): ok this hits most boxes. we'll do the pilot but need the security docs and the pricing.
07:15 Speaker 1 (Samira): noted — samira will send docs. liam will draft pilot config.
07:20 Speaker 5 (Ellen): one process note — we'll want the benchmark to integrate with our metrics dashboard; do you have a prometheus or datadog exporter?
07:26 Speaker 4 (Liam): yes, we have exporters and HTTP webhooks for metrics. we'll add the spec to the checklist.
07:33 Speaker 1 (Samira): cool. any remaining blockers?
07:35 Speaker 2 (Maya): just finalizing the prompt set and the redaction golden labels; we'll deliver that by monday.
07:39 Speaker 3 (Ravi): i'll confirm HSM needs and raise any policy exceptions.
07:43 Speaker 1 (Samira): brilliant — recap and next steps: send pricing and security pack, liam to send benchmark checklist, customer to provide 200-sample prompts and pass/fail criteria, schedule pilot kickoff for week of 12/29.
07:56 Speaker 2 (Maya): thanks everyone, excited to try it.
08:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): thanks all, we'll follow up in email.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions ("vac-cache" instead of KV cache, some model names normalized). natural speech, interruptions, and slight repetition present.

References mentioned: pricing deck (link withheld), security pack (to be attached), pilot checklist (Liam will share), sample prompt CSV template (Samira will attach).

End of transcript.
